method.note: Live authorities remain canonical. This artifact is a compact research snapshot. US, Canada, Australia and ECB FX are required preflight inputs. NZ and Japan are not required_for_trader_preflight; a blocked RBNZ source or a Japan holiday-calendar print stays visible on that source and does not by itself mark the packet stale. NZ-dependent and JP-dependent expressions still fail closed. The official RBNZ B2 XLSX is tried first, including a browser-TLS retry, then the official RBNZ B2 HTML table. No vendor or media substitute is used. Japan JGB freshness uses the Tokyo business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. Euro-area Bund (Germany) and Japan JGB cash curves remain six-economy rate legs. Cross-country spreads use exact common observation dates only. Policy-path context uses official overnight benchmarks plus public money-market data. The required tradable paper rates universe remains SOFR via CME SR3, CORRA via MX CRA, and AONIA via ASX IB. TONA is included when JPX OSE 3M settlements pass identity checks; FST3/€STR stays observe_only until a public settlement feed is reliable. Official government zero/forward curves are supplemental bond-curve inputs and are not required to manufacture a swap curve. Euro-area sovereign fragmentation (IT/FR/ES vs Bund) is market context, never an EA temperature input. Housing context is collected for the US, Canada and Australia from free maintained public sources: FHFA/Census/Fed/Freddie Mac via FRED for the US, Statistics Canada/CMHC/Bank of Canada for Canada, and ABS/RBA for Australia. EA/JP housing is omitted until an official/free source meets the contract. CFTC TFF supplies trader-class ownership/crowding context and can mark the packet stale. CME's public volume/open-interest service is a supplemental overlay and does not flip packet status. No historical warehouse is written to GitHub or Supabase.

items.headline: Fed Used Treasury Funds to Support Yen in Joint Intervention
items.summary: The Federal Reserve said US participation with Japan in intervening to support the yen in late July was a Treasury Department move, and that its own funds were not used.

items.headline: Robert Rubin Warns AI Boom Carries Risks for US Economy, Markets
items.summary: Former Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin warned that the artificial-intelligence investment boom could bring major productivity gains but also create financial and social risks.

items.headline: Mideast Oil Chiefs Warn World Needs to Share Iran-War Costs
items.summary: The heads of two of the Middle East's biggest oil producers warned that the rest of the world will need to share the burden of paying for the Iran war and infrastructure spending.

items.headline: Czech Inflation Breaches Target as Policymakers Mull More Hikes
items.summary: Czech inflation accelerated more than expected last month after the central bank warned that tighter monetary policy may be warranted.

items.headline: Ray Dalio Warns China, Japan May Pull Back From Treasuries
items.summary: Ray Dalio warned that the US Treasury market is vulnerable to a pullback of demand from China and Japan.

items.headline: Global Oil Supply Buffer Running 'Scarily Thin,' Aramco CEO Says
items.summary: The oil stockpiles that cushion the world from supply shocks have become scarily thin unless the Strait of Hormuz reopens, according to Aramco's CEO.

items.headline: Iran's Oil Minister Resigns as Exports Dry Up Under US Pressure
items.summary: Iran's oil minister resigned citing personal reasons as the Islamic Republic tries to sustain its oil industry under a tightening US blockade.

items.headline: LNG Trade Through Hormuz Extends Rebound Despite Shipping Risks
items.summary: Shipments of LNG through the Strait of Hormuz extended a rebound that began in September.

items.headline: Euro-Zone Inflation Tops Estimates to Hit Three-Year High
items.summary: Euro-area inflation quickened more than expected to the highest in three years.

items.headline: UK Firms Predict Faster Price Increases After Energy Costs Surge
items.summary: The resurgence in oil and gas prices drove up UK businesses' inflation expectations as firms planned to pass on cost increases.

items.headline: Pimco's Stracke Says AI Spending Drove Yields, Not Inflation
items.summary: Surging capital demand from hyperscalers and the AI ecosystem—not inflation expectations—is the primary force pushing real rates and bond yields higher, Pimco's Stracke said.

items.headline: China Oil Comeback Loses Steam as Iran War Drags On
items.summary: A nascent recovery in Chinese oil demand has begun to falter as the Middle East conflict and limited Iranian supply keep crude prices high.

items.headline: Man Group Says 5.5% Yields Risk Cracking AI Capex, US Consumer
items.summary: Man Group's Kristina Hooper warned that surging long-end Treasury yields threaten AI capital expenditures and US consumer resilience.

items.headline: Hungarian Central Banker Floats 2031 Euro Adoption Scenario
items.summary: Hungary could adopt the euro as early as 2031 if the government set an ambitious goal of meeting the criteria by 2029, according to Deputy Governor Zoltan Kurali.

items.headline: Google, Constellation Near Billion-Dollar Deal for Nuclear Power
items.summary: Google parent Alphabet is close to an agreement to buy nuclear energy from Constellation Energy.

items.headline: Lescure Says France Is Far From Needing ECB Help on Debt
items.summary: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure said the country is far from needing the ECB to step in even as it wrestles with soaring bond yields.
